bindings.note: No UF rule reads the key: RuleHandleCabinetUrbanFreestanding shows the grooves from Height (82 without, 88 with), so the handle reaches the scene as the height it forces (cabinet table). Sent so the scene config keeps the handle, which the player reads back for the selected cabinet. UF_Cabinet has no Central Groove mesh (UF_HandleBotCut_Top).

Number in cm, plinth included: 91 for Upper and Central Groove, 88 for Push-to-Open (cabinet table). The UF rules lay out two drawers at 82 (no grooves) and 88 (grooves) only: at 91 they do nothing, so the cabinet keeps its template shape, and 88 shows grooves. Not translated: the player and the scene state reader take the height back from the scene config (I04), so a scene number would replace the catalog height in state and pricing. Waits for the scene to take 88 and 91.
Number in cm, set on one cabinet. RuleWidthCabinetUrbanFreestanding takes 25, 35, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100, 105 and 120, every width of the cabinet table.

Number in cm, one depth for the composition. RuleDepthCabinetUrbanFreestanding lays out 45 and 50 only; the cabinet table lists 46 (price list), which the scene leaves at the 50 cm geometry until it takes 46. Not translated, for the reason given for Height.

Urban Freestanding has two drawers (2DW) only. The UF scene draws them from Height without reading the key; sent in the legacy spelling, as Urban Standard Height sends it, because history and saved configurations read the style from the scene config.

The PlayCanvas material name, as in Urban Standard Height. No UF rule paints it yet: the global RuleChangeCabinetColor paints Urban Standard Height mesh names, none of which UF_Cabinet has, so the UF cabinets keep their template material until the scene paints them.

The countertop is placed at composition level (global RuleChangeCountertopColor); the UF cabinets ignore the key. Countertop table 589 has the rows of Urban Standard Height's 438, so its Syntesi finishes reuse the Tekorlux scene materials as there (TAL/TAM, not TAN/TAP).
Read by the countertop. Only 0.5 is offered; UF-sink-cabinet declares no basin offsets by thickness.

The Urban Standard Height basin names, sent to every UF Sink Base. UF-sink-cabinet takes its basin sub-product from sinkType when it is placed but has no RuleChangeSinkType, so a later change stays in its config without swapping the basin until the scene adds the rule. "Vessel" is the scene placeholder for a vessel countertop without a basin.
